officialProductPage.evidence: Official model-specific 25-26 page. Identifies CT as a carving-oriented all-round directional camber board for beginner through expert riders; states a 25-26 sidewall change for standard sizes and gives a complete geometry table for 10 standard sizes and 3 wide sizes.

priceJPY.note: Japanese domestic list prices, including the displayed tax-inclusive prices. These are not China-market prices. Existing seed CNY 4856 is a project FX-normalized estimate based on the standard tax-inclusive JPY 114400, not a verified Chinese offer.

officialProductPage.productCopySummary: The maker describes a forgiving, relatively soft-flexing all-round carving board with a broad sweet spot and easy turning, aimed from beginner through expert. The 25-26 standard model changes its sidewall to slightly strengthen grip; wide sizes are unchanged. This is manufacturer positioning, not independent test evidence.

officialLinkedSeasonCatalog.hostNote: The catalog is linked directly from the official OGASAKA Snowboard website's news as its 25-26 user catalog, but the page content is hosted on snowboardnet.jp rather than the brand domain.
officialLinkedSeasonCatalog.evidence: The season-specific CT catalog page lists NV Core, Glass Fiber Carbon Composite, Type-S PC plate for 143-161 and Type-OG1 for 154W-158W, consistent with the model-specific 25-26 official product page.

officialTechnologyPage.evidence: The general technology page maps CT to BX Core and CT 158W to BX2 Core, and gives a different PC Plate model mapping from the 25-26 CT product-specific page. It does not expose a season-specific revision date.
officialTechnologyPage.resolution: This undated general page maps CT differently (BX Core and other PC plate groupings), but both season-specific 25-26 sources—the model product page and OGASAKA-linked 25-26 catalog—agree on NV Core and the season-specific PC plate mapping. Use those values for the 25-26 seed; retain the generic-page discrepancy as a non-season-specific caveat rather than an unresolved target-season fact.

natoriRideReview2026.title: 新型「CT」フレックス調整で何が変わった？OGASAKAボード解説
natoriRideReview2026.hostNote: Practitioner ride commentary summarized from the author's video, not a standardized multi-rider test. The author profile notes employment with a snowboard manufacturer and subsequent snowboard-brand business; treat the review as informed but not independent laboratory evidence.
natoriRideReview2026.testBoard: CT 158 cm, with the rider using a 520 mm stance versus the listed 560 mm reference stance. The article discusses the new CT from the current season, so 2025/26 is inferred from publication context; it does not print an explicit factory model-year label.
natoriRideReview2026.conditionsAndDuration: Exact test date, number of runs/days, snow conditions, and rider body/boot specifications are not disclosed.
natoriRideReview2026.observations: Compared with the prior CT feel, the tester describes the new board as more compliant/supple and easier to handle while retaining edge grip. They report improved snow-following and less chatter in rough snow, stable turns, and confidence at speed. These are one rider's qualitative impressions, not measured performance values.
natoriRideReview2026.notTestedOrNotEstablished: No direct powder, park/jump, or controlled forgiveness assessment is provided; do not use the article to calibrate float or park scores or to transfer size-158 specifications/fit to the seed's representative 156.
natoriRideReview2026.authorBackground: The author profile states snowboard-manufacturer employment beginning in 2004, followed by founding a snowboard-related business in 2010; useful expertise context, but also a reason to retain source/independence caveats.

scoringEvidence.decision: Retain all six existing editorial scores. Two companion writeups by the same practitioner on 2026-04-16 describe riding CT 158 during the current-season Tangram demo period; with the 25-26 context, the evidence is season-consistent but the articles do not print an explicit factory model year. They directionally support strong edge grip, rough-snow composure, stability and easier handling, but are not independent replications, use size 158 rather than the seed's 156, and omit CT-specific test duration and exact conditions. They give no direct powder or park evaluation. Do not map qualitative language to score deltas or any external rating scale.
